description: Two stacked panels of the same type — misorientation distribution functions (EBSD-derived grain-boundary-character plots) — sharing identical axes: Frequency (linear, 0 to 0.35, ticks every 0.05) on the y-axis and Misorientation angle (°) (0 to 65, ticks every 5°) on the x-axis. Neither panel carries a printed (a)/(b) letter. In each panel a red vertical line at 15° separates the region labelled LAB (to its left) from that labelled HAB (to its right). Top panel: the curve is highest at the lowest plotted angles (about 0.31 near 3°), decays steeply to the baseline by ~12° and remains flat out to 65°; printed text reads "LAB : 85%", "HAB : 15%", "Average angle : 9,4°". Bottom panel: the curve peaks near 0.13 at low angles, decays slowly, and retains a broad, low maximum around 45–48° (roughly 0.01–0.02) before falling to about zero near 58–60°; printed text reads "LAB : 47%", "HAB : 53%", "Average angle : 23,7°". The caption states these distributions are for 1000 °C and 0.1 s⁻¹ and mentions ε = 25. Together the panels demonstrate the strain-driven shift from a strongly LAB-dominated misorientation distribution to one in which subgrain and grain boundaries are balanced.

observations.observation: Both panels plot Frequency (y-axis, 0 to 0.35, ticks every 0.05) against Misorientation angle in degrees (x-axis, 0 to 65, ticks every 5).
A red vertical line at 15° divides each panel into a left region labelled LAB and a right region labelled HAB.

In the top panel the curve reaches its maximum of about 0.31 at the lowest plotted angles (near 3°), falls to the baseline by about 12°, and remains flat to 65°; the panel prints 'LAB : 85%', 'HAB : 15%', 'Average angle : 9,4°'.

In the bottom panel the curve starts near 0.13, decays slowly, and retains a broad low maximum around 45–48° at roughly 0.01–0.02 before falling to zero near 58–60°; the panel prints 'LAB : 47%', 'HAB : 53%', 'Average angle : 23,7°'.
Both curves are plotted to the same y-scale, so the top-panel distribution is markedly more concentrated at low misorientation angles than the bottom-panel one.
The caption states the misorientation distribution functions correspond to 1000 °C and 0.1 s⁻¹.
The caption states a strain value of ε = 25 for this figure.
The citing text attributes the large fraction of misorientations below 15° at low strain (Fig. 2a) to the continuous creation of subgrain boundaries.

The citing text states that the amount of misorientation between 15 and 62.8° increases significantly with strain, attributed to the progressive transformation of subgrain boundaries into grain boundaries.
The citing text states that at large strain (Fig. 2b) there is a balance between the amount of subgrain and grain boundaries, matching the printed HAB : 53% / LAB : 47% split.
Neither panel carries a printed (a) or (b) letter, so the correspondence of the top/bottom panel to the low-strain/high-strain cases is inferred from the citing text rather than the image.

subfigures.description: Misorientation distribution function, Frequency (0–0.35) vs Misorientation angle (0–65°), with a red vertical divider at 15° labelled LAB (left) and HAB (right). The curve peaks near 0.31 at the smallest angles, falls to the baseline by about 12° and stays flat. Printed values: LAB : 85%, HAB : 15%, Average angle : 9,4°.

Same axes and same red 15° LAB/HAB divider. The curve starts at about 0.13, decays slowly, and shows a broad low maximum near 45–48° (about 0.01–0.02) before dropping to zero near 60°. Printed values: LAB : 47%, HAB : 53%, Average angle : 23,7°.
